schema.purpose: Ground truth for where rubber is deposited on the ground during the beat-2 launch and the beat-3/4 drive out. Geometry and deposit profile ONLY -- no shader, no mesh. Authored from world/car_anim_car.json (the built car) + telemetry/telemetry.csv.
schema.frame_of_reference: Blender world metres, +Z up. film_frame is the 1-based film frame at 24 fps; world_t is telemetry seconds via anim/filmtime.py (NOT film_t - 34.0718 past beat 3's ramp).
schema.wheels: FL/FR/RL/RR contact-patch tracks. RL/RR are the driven pair and are the only ones that carry deposit; FL/FR are included for completeness and carry deposit_norm = 0 everywhere (no lockup exists in this film).

arrays.world_t: telemetry seconds at that film frame, through anim/filmtime.py
arrays.x,y,z: contact-patch centre in world metres; z is the ground height under the patch from carrig's four-wheel contact solve
arrays.s_along_track_m: cumulative 3D arc length along this wheel's own track from the first sample (film frame 793)
arrays.deposit_norm: rubber mass deposited per unit track length, normalised so the peak over this wheel's track is 1.0. It is a PER-SEGMENT quantity credited to the segment ENDING at this sample.
arrays.slip_velocity_ms: tyre surface speed minus ground speed at the contact patch, m/s, over the segment ending at this sample
arrays.slip_distance_m: metres of tyre surface slid over the ground in the segment ending at this sample
arrays.surface_id: one of dais_deck | delivery_ramp | showroom_floor | apron
arrays.normal_load_norm: vertical load on THIS wheel as a fraction of the car's weight (static split + longitudinal transfer)

schema.consumer_note: For the launch marks use `launch_mark` (the headline numbers) and `launch_mark_profile` (a 256-point d(s) resample). The per-frame arrays are sampled at ~2 cm through the mark, which is 11 stair steps; the resample is the smooth one.

rolling_radius_note: 0.360 EXACTLY, and it is not a fit. (a) anim/carrig.py measures the modelled tyre off world/beat1_anim.blend at 0.70000 - 0.34002 = 0.35998 m. (b) the telemetry is CONSTRUCTED as wheel_rot_rad = s_m/0.36 + slip: the residual wheel_rot_rad - s_m/0.36 has sd 8.0e-05 rad and peak-to-peak 2.8e-04 rad over all 1683 no-slip rows, and 2.8e-04 rad is exactly one unit of the CSV's 4-dp quantisation of s_m (0.0001/0.36). (c) d(world arc)/d(wheel_rot) = 0.360034 to 0.360040 over every long no-slip stretch, the 1e-4 excess being the leg-0 stretch and chord/arc polygonisation. A rolling radius of 0.378 makes the same residual drift to 545 rad over the lap and is rejected.

slip_summary.slip_elsewhere_in_the_lap: NONE. Outside the launch the per-row change in the declared slip never exceeds 2.8e-04 rad = 0.101 mm of tyre surface per frame, which is the CSV's own 4-dp rounding of s_m and not motion. There is no corner-exit wheelspin and no braking lockup anywhere in the 72.58 s of telemetry: the telemetry declares EXACT rolling contact everywhere except the sanctioned launch window.
slip_summary.deposit_model: dm/dt = k*mu*Fz*v_slip (frictional-power wear), so per metre of ground dm/ds = k*mu*Fz*v_slip/v_car = k*mu*Fz*(R*d_slip)/d_ground. k and mu are constant over the 11 frames on one surface and cancel in the normalisation. Fz is the static rear split (0.55) plus longitudinal transfer m*a_x*h_cg/L with h_cg = 0.30 m.

RL.decay_note: The 1 % figure is CLAMPED to the mark length: the deposit never decays to 1 %, it terminates at 2.7 % of peak when the tyre hooks up. The mark has a hard trailing edge, not a fade.

RR.decay_note: The 1 % figure is CLAMPED to the mark length: the deposit never decays to 1 %, it terminates at 2.7 % of peak when the tyre hooks up. The mark has a hard trailing edge, not a fade.

as_derived.lateral_error_note: 77.5 mm inboard of the tyre. That is inside the 0.32 m feather but OUTSIDE the 0.10 m core, so the tyre runs on the shoulder of its own mark, not its heart -- the same class of defect as R2-651, three orders of magnitude smaller.

All 3.2903 m of tyre-surface slip in this film happens at x = -1.793..-1.558, on the turntable deck, before the car has moved 25 cm. The painted apron streaks are not supported by the telemetry at any strength, let alone full strength at the glass.

q1_lateral.where_is_u_zero: uv_su u == V, the signed lateral offset from the ACCESS ROUTE centreline (build_surface._build_access: PX = X1 - sin(H)*V, PY = Y1 + cos(H)*V, uv_su = [V, T]). world_contract.access_route_point(t) = (15.0+t, 0.0, 0.0) for t <= ACCESS_L2 = 49.60, measured max |y| = 0.0e+00 m and max |heading| = 0.0e+00 rad over the painted span. So on this span u = 0 IS world y = 0 and u IS world y. The 77.5 mm is REAL, not a coordinate-frame artefact.

RL.sign_convention: positive = the tyre runs OUTBOARD of the painted centre

RR.sign_convention: positive = the tyre runs OUTBOARD of the painted centre

q1_lateral.verdict: The paint is centred 77.5 mm INBOARD of both rear tyres, identically at every sample (the car runs dead straight on y = 0 here, so there is no scatter at all: p50 = max). That is inside the 0.32 m feather but outside the 0.10 m core, so each tyre runs on the OUTBOARD SHOULDER of its own mark rather than its heart.

q2_longitudinal.verdict: CONFIRMED, and it is the headline. Slip velocity over the entire painted span is EXACTLY 0.0 m/s -- not small, zero: the rig makes rolling contact exact by construction outside the launch window (carrig.spin = ground_distance/0.36 + slip, and slip is flat there). The car passes x = 15 at 16.214 m/s and x = 49 at 31.395 m/s with the wheels fully hooked up. 0.0 of the deposit lies at x >= 15; 100 % of it lies on the turntable deck at x = -1.793 ..-1.558. The existing paint covers 34 m where no rubber is laid, and nothing paints the 0.24 m where all of it is.

q3_width.source: ~/opus5-car-render/build/spec.py + s04_car.tyre_profile (READ ONLY). TYRE_R = 0.360 -- which independently confirms the rolling radius from the mesh. REAR_TYRE_Y = 1.000 - 0.2025 = 0.79750, exactly carrig.HALF_TRACK_REAR, so the track figures ARE the tyre centre planes.
q3_width.tread_definition: tyre_profile() holds the full radius TYRE_R over axial +-hw*0.620 and then steps the shoulder down 0.5 mm at 0.772, 4.0 mm at 0.876 and 18 mm at 0.950 of hw. The contact solve is rigid (no tyre deflection), so the patch is the flat tread.
q3_width.verdict: Rear contact patch is 251.1 mm wide, |y| = 0.67195..0.92305 -- NOT the 400 mm assumed. The painted 200 mm core (|y| 0.62..0.82) is 20 % too narrow AND offset, so it covers only 148.0 mm of the 251.1 mm tread (59.0 %), and 103 mm of the outboard tread gets feather only. Front, for completeness: 189.1 mm wide at |y| = 0.75295..0.94205.
